1	# Lumen AI Agent Guidelines (`AGENTS.md`)
2	
3	This guide provides instructions, architectural rules, engineering invariants, and task runner workflows for AI coding agents (Antigravity, Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Codex) working on the Lumen codebase.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Repository Architecture & Crate Layers
8	
9	Lumen is a multi-orchestrator telemetry, session intelligence, and token economics engine written in Rust. It is structured into strict architectural layers:
10	
11	```text
12	┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
13	│                          LUMEN CRATE LAYERS                            │
14	├───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┤
15	│ LAYER & CRATE                     │ LICENSE & PURPOSE                  │
16	├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
17	│ Layer 1: lumen-model              │ MIT / Apache-2.0                   │
18	│                                   │ Canonical IR & Pricing Matrix      │
19	├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
20	│ Layer 1.5: lumen-session          │ MIT / Apache-2.0                   │
21	│                                   │ Streaming Ingestion & Adapters     │
22	├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
23	│ Layer 2: lumen-analysis           │ FSL-1.1-MIT                        │
24	│          lumen-pattern            │ 22 Accumulators, Trajectory DAG    │
25	├───────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
26	│ Layer 4: lumen-cli                │ FSL-1.1-MIT                        │
27	│                                   │ Standalone CLI & Telemetry Tools   │
28	└───────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
29	```
30	
31	> **CRITICAL RULE (Layer Licensing Boundaries)**: Layer 1 (`lumen-model`) and Layer 1.5 (`lumen-session`) MUST NOT depend on Layer 2 or Layer 4 crates (`lumen-analysis`, `lumen-pattern`, `lumen-cli`). Layer 1/1.5 crates must remain permissive (`MIT OR Apache-2.0`) and standalone.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Primary Task Runners & Verification Pipelines
36	
37	Always use `just` or `moon` task runners for building, testing, linting, and formatting.
38	
39	| Action | Primary Task Runner Command | Moon Engine Command |
40	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
41	| **Run Full Verification CI** | `just ci` | `moon run :format-check && moon run :lint && moon run :test` |
42	| **Run Test Suite** | `just test` | `moon run :test` |
43	| **Check Clippy Lints** | `just lint` | `moon run :lint` |
44	| **Check Formatting** | `just fmt-check` | `moon run :format-check` |
45	| **Format Code** | `just fmt` | `moon run :format` |
46	
47	---
48	
49	## 3. Strict Engineering Invariants
50	
51	1. **Safe Rust Only (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`)**: `unsafe` code blocks are strictly forbidden across all workspace crates.
52	2. **Deterministic Token Accounting**: Token calculations must account for uncached input, 5m ephemeral write, 1h write, 0.10x cache read discount, and output tokens without division by zero.
53	3. **Linear Streaming Pass $O(N)$**: Telemetry accumulators must operate in a single linear pass over the canonical turns without nested heap allocations.

Build is currently clean across the workspace. Here's the picture of what Lumen is and where it stands.

## What Lumen is

A Rust workspace that parses AI coding-agent transcript logs (Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex, OpenCode), normalizes them into a canonical IR, computes exact prompt-cache economics (Anthropic's 4-tier pricing), and detects circular tool-call loops via Tarjan SCC on a trajectory graph.

**Layered crates** (strict one-way dependency, enforced by license boundary):
- `lumen-model` (L1, MIT/Apache-2.0) — canonical IR, turn/transcript types, pricing matrix
- `lumen-session` (L1.5, MIT/Apache-2.0) — streaming SIMD adapters per orchestrator (fingerprint detection, snapshot merging)
- `lumen-analysis` + `lumen-pattern` (L2, FSL-1.1-MIT) — 22 single-pass accumulators + petgraph trajectory DAG/cycle detection
- `lumen-store` — SQLite WAL repository layer (untracked, in progress)
- `lumen-cli` (L4, FSL-1.1-MIT) — CLI/TUI entrypoint (`audit`, `trace`, `scan`)

Governing invariants from `AGENTS.md`: no `unsafe`, deterministic token accounting, O(N) single-pass accumulators, no emoji in code/docs, and L1/L1.5 must never depend on L2/L4.

## Specs vs. implementation status

8 specs exist (`SPEC-LUMEN-001` through `008`), covering model, session, store, daemon, analysis, pattern, insights, CLI. Only 3 have plans (`PLAN-LUMEN-001-MODEL`, `002-SESSION`, `005-ANALYSIS`) — no plans yet for store, daemon, pattern, insights, or CLI.

Your git status shows active untracked work: a large batch of new accumulators (`artifacts`, `autonomy`, `context_growth`, `permission_mode`, `stats`, `tool_inventory`), new tests across analysis/model/pattern/session, the entire `lumen-store` crate, an OpenCode adapter, plus tooling (`justfile`, `moon.yml`, `.rustfmt.toml`, `.clippy.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.prototools`). None of this is committed yet.

Want me to dig into a specific spec (e.g. `SPEC-LUMEN-004-DAEMON` or `007-INSIGHTS`, which have no plan yet), or check what's actually implemented against `SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS`'s 22-accumulator list vs. what's in `accumulators/`?

These docs were put together from a combination of research from Claude and Antigravity with a Gemini model and might need a round of analysis and deep research to validate that we're going in the right direction and we've thought things through.

This calls for a real audit pass, not a quick read — checking whether the docs' technical claims hold up against the actual code, whether the specs are rigorous, and whether the more speculative docs (Swift app blueprint, commercial strategy, "six generational leaps") are grounded or just hype. I'll fork four parallel research passes and synthesize.

## Bottom line

The **foundation is real** — `lumen-model`, `lumen-session`, and the core of `lumen-analysis` are legitimately implemented, tested, and mostly match their specs. But **the docs suite as a whole significantly overclaims the system's current state**, and one specific claim (README benchmarks) is fabricated in a way that should be fixed immediately.

## What's solid

- **Pricing/cache economics** (doc 01): formula is correct for the 3 tiers actually tracked, div-by-zero is guarded. It claims a 4th tier ("1h write") that's hardcoded to `0` in `economics.rs` — stubbed, not implemented.
- **Adapters** (doc 02): Claude Code, AGY, Codex, and OpenCode all exist as real parsers (not stubs), fingerprint detection is tested.
- **lumen-store**: WAL mode and read-only pragma are real and match the spec. Roughly matches SPEC-003's API surface.
- Everything that *is* built has real test coverage backing it.

## The core gaps

**"22 accumulators" is the headline gap.** Only 11 accumulator files exist, only 10 are wired into the engine (`schema_extractor.rs` is built but never registered — dead code). 9 of the 22 named in the README, doc 03, and SPEC-005 don't exist at all: `flow`, `hook_activity`, `pr_link`, `fuzzy_tools`, `attribution`, `timeline`, `otel_correlation`, `span_mapping`, `trajectory_dag`. SPEC-005 itself only defines acceptance criteria for 8 of the 22, and PLAN-005 orphans 4 more criteria that are in the spec but covered by no task.

**Tarjan SCC cycle detection is currently inert.** The algorithm is correctly implemented against the stated invariant (depth ≥3, identical target symbol, zero mutation), but the only public convenience entry point never populates `target_symbol`, so it can never actually fire end-to-end right now.

**The daemon is 100% vaporware.** Zero matching code anywhere in the repo — no crate, no plan, nothing. `SPEC-004-DAEMON`'s entire API surface is fiction. This cascades: doc 08's Swift Mac app depends on a daemon that doesn't exist; `SPEC-003-STORE` references a "Mac app read contract" with no schema in the repo to test against; `SPEC-004` requires store insert methods `SPEC-003` never defines.

**The CLI is a small fraction of what's specced.** Real code only has `trace`/`audit`/`scan`. `anstream`/`indicatif` are claimed in doc 05 but unused. `SPEC-008-CLI` describes `status`, `refresh`, `sessions`, `insights`, `weekly`, `export`, `doctor`, `daemon`, `--toon` output, IPC — none of it exists (~90% fictional relative to code).

**README benchmark numbers are fabricated.** No `criterion` dependency, no `bench/` directory anywhere. "1.5 GB/s SIMD," "31.4ms/50MB," "0.4ms Tarjan on 500 nodes," and the entire comparative matrix vs. OpenTelemetry/Phoenix/LangSmith are unmeasured numbers presented as measured results in a public README. This is the single most important item to fix — it's a credibility risk, not just a docs gap.

content.text:
This is a much bigger job than it first looked — two of the three crates are substantially unfinished relative to their specs, and several pieces require real design decisions before I write code. Quick picture of what I found:

**prism-core**: drivers (Claude/AGY/OpenAI-compatible/OpenCode/VCR) are solidly implemented. `WorkspaceSandbox` is a stub — just `cp -r` + `git init`, missing the spec'd Reflink/APFS CoW cloning, POSIX process-group reaping/timeout, and `git_checkout`/`apply_patch`/`run_test_suite` methods entirely. Also found a real bug: `OpenCodeDriver` parses OpenCode's output with `ClaudeCodeAdapter` instead of the `OpenCodeAdapter` that now exists in lumen-session.

**prism-grader**: 3 of 4 graders exist (RedGreen, Trajectory, CircuitBreaker) but `RedGreenGrader` doesn't actually implement the `Grader` trait the spec defines. `CalibratedJudge` (the Opus rubric grader) doesn't exist at all — zero code.

**prism-cli**: this is the roughest part. `prism test` builds a fake in-memory transcript with empty turns and never invokes any real driver or sandbox. `prism bench` prints **hardcoded literal numbers** ("62.5%", "$0.42") — not computed from anything. `prism rebuild` and `prism record` are pure `println!` stubs. `prism matrix` — the subcommand the spec requires — doesn't exist in the CLI at all, even though `MatrixResultDatum`/`MetricDifferential` are already built in prism-grader. No TOML config loading, no suite-file format/loader, no OTel/Parquet/GitHub-summary exporters exist (`toml` is a declared dependency but unused; there's no `opentelemetry` or `parquet` dependency at all). And `rebuild` as a command has zero corresponding acceptance criteria anywhere in the specs — it's pure invention sitting in the code.

Given the size and the number of real design decisions in here (how `CalibratedJudge` actually calls out to Claude, what the matrix/suite TOML schemas look like, whether to build OTel/Parquet now or stub them, what to do with the unspec'd `rebuild` command), I want to lay out a sequenced plan before writing code rather than starting to type.

1	# Prism Architecture: Core Evaluation Models, VCR Cassettes & Sandboxing (`01-core-evaluation-and-vcr-cassettes.md`)
2	
3	This document defines the core evaluation data models, VCR cassette record/replay engine, and workspace sandboxing in `crates/prism-core`.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Domain Models
8	
9	```rust
10	pub struct TaskSpec {
11	    pub id: CompactString,
12	    pub skill: CompactString,
13	    pub input_prompt: String,
14	    pub fixture_repo: Option<PathBuf>,
15	    pub expected_assertions: Vec<CompactString>,
16	    pub max_turns: usize,
17	    pub timeout_seconds: u64,
18	}
19	
20	pub struct VcrCassette {
21	    pub task_id: CompactString,
22	    pub prompt_hash: CompactString,
23	    pub transcript: CanonicalTranscript,
24	}
25	```
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 2. Execution Drivers
30	
31	1. **`ClaudeCliDriver` / `AgyCliDriver`**: Spawns local CLI in non-interactive mode. Zero API keys needed; uses developer's active login session.
32	2. **`AnthropicApiDriver`**: Direct HTTPS Messages API with `anthropic-beta: prompt-caching-2024-07-31` headers.
33	3. **`VcrReplayDriver`**: Replays frozen cassettes in $<5\text{ms}$ with $\$0.00$ API spend.

36	
37	## 3. Hermetic Sandboxing (`WorkspaceSandbox`)
38	
39	- Clones fixture repository into isolated `/tmp/prism_sandbox_*/` directory.
40	- Initializes clean ephemeral Git repository.
41	- Evaluates test state transitions without polluting host workspace.
42	- Cleans up automatically on drop.

1	# Prism Architecture: The 4 Decoupled Evaluation Grader Engines (`02-the-four-grader-engines.md`)

3	This document defines the 4 evaluation grading engines in `crates/prism-grader`.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Grader Engine Architecture
8	
9	```rust
10	pub trait Grader: Send + Sync {
11	    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
12	    fn evaluate(
13	        &self,
14	        spec: &TaskSpec,
15	        transcript: &CanonicalTranscript,
16	    ) -> Result<AssertionResult, EvaluationError>;
17	}
18	```

23	
24	1. **`RedGreenGrader`**: SWE-bench style state transition verification. Asserts test suite FAILS before patch (Red Pass) and PASSES with zero regressions after patch (Green Pass).
25	2. **`TrajectoryGrader`**: Asserts prompt cache hit ratio $\ge 90.0\%$ and zero circular Tarjan SCC exploration loops.
26	3. **`CircuitBreakerGrader`**: Asserts multi-agent review iterations (Drafter ↔ Auditor) reach consensus in $\le 2$ rounds.
27	4. **`CalibratedJudge`**: Evaluates formative G-Eval rubrics with Opus using contrastive pass/fail few-shot anchors.

4

1	# Multi-Dimensional Matrix Evaluation & Empirical Differentials (`docs/04`)
2	
3	This document defines the 8 empirical evaluation dimensions, Cartesian matrix execution engine, and statistical percentage differential ($\Delta$) formulas of Prism.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. The 8 Evaluated Dimensions
8	
9	Prism evaluates every trial across 8 empirical dimensions:
10	
11	| Dimension | Metric Unit | Calculation Formula | Purpose |
12	| :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
13	| **1. Pass Rate** | `%` | `(passed_assertions / total_assertions) * 100.0` | Functional correctness & zero regressions. |
14	| **2. Cache Hit Ratio** | `%` | $H = \frac{I_{\text{read}}}{I_{\text{uncached}} + I_{\text{write}} + I_{\text{read}}} \times 100.0$ | Prompt cache health & prefix stability. |
15	| **3. Financial Cost** | `USD $` | Exact 4-tier spend ($P_{\text{in}}, P_{\text{write}}, P_{\text{read}}, P_{\text{out}}$) | Monetary cost per task trial. |
16	| **4. Turns** | `Count` | Total user, assistant, and tool turns | Directness of resolution vs wandering. |
17	| **5. Turn Latency** | `ms` | p50 & p95 percentiles of turn completions | API responsiveness and tool overhead. |
18	| **6. Total Wall Time** | `ms` / `s` | $\sum_{t=1}^N \text{latency}(t)$ | Total developer wait time. |
19	| **7. Token Volumes** | `Tokens` | Total prompt input + completion output | Context inflation & prompt verbosity. |
20	| **8. Quality Score** | `[0.0 - 1.0]` | Grounding ($\mathcal{G}$) + Monotonicity ($M$) + Rubric | Solution elegance & zero cyclic loops. |
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 2. Same-vs-Same Empirical Differentials
25	
26	To eliminate anecdotal guessing, Prism calculates exact percentage deltas ($\Delta$) against baseline controls:
27	
28	```rust
29	// crates/prism-grader/src/matrix.rs
30	pub struct MetricDifferential {
31	    pub delta_pass_rate_pct: f32,    // e.g. +36.0%
32	    pub delta_cost_pct: f32,         // e.g. -66.7% (Savings)
33	    pub delta_turns_pct: f32,        // e.g. -63.4% (Fewer turns)
34	    pub delta_cache_hit_pct: f32,    // e.g. +49.3% (Higher cache hit)
35	    pub delta_latency_p95_pct: f32,  // e.g. -42.1% (Faster turns)
36	    pub delta_wall_time_pct: f32,    // e.g. -55.0% (Faster completion)
37	    pub delta_quality_score_pct: f32,// e.g. +22.5% (Higher quality)
38	}
39	```
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Commercial API vs. Self-Hosted Zero-Token Costing
44	
45	* **Commercial APIs**: Exact 4-tier billing per million tokens ($P_{\text{in}}, P_{\text{write}}, P_{\text{read}}, P_{\text{out}}$).
46	* **Local & On-Prem Models (Qwen, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM)**: Reported as **`$0.00 (API Token Fees) / Self-Hosted`**, while tracking real physical compute metrics (Wall Time, Latency p95, Token Volumes, and Turns).

# Lumen: Comprehensive Spec/Doc Gap-Filling

## Context

An earlier 4-way audit (core code vs. docs, infra/CLI vs. docs, adversarial spec quality, strategy-doc scrutiny) found that Lumen's specs and docs systematically overclaim relative to what's built and, in several places, are internally inconsistent or untestable as written:

- **SPEC-005-ANALYSIS**: only 8 of the "22 accumulators" have acceptance criteria at all (some implemented accumulators like `artifacts`/`autonomy`/`context_growth`/`stats`/`tool_inventory` aren't even covered; 9 more — `flow`, `hook_activity`, `pr_link`, `fuzzy_tools`, `attribution`, `timeline`, `otel_correlation`, `span_mapping`, `trajectory_dag` — don't exist as code or criteria). PLAN-005 orphans 4 criteria that are in the spec but in no task.
- **SPEC-002-SESSION**: CodexAdapter and OpenCodeAdapter have zero acceptance criteria despite being claimed "multi-orchestrator" support. The 50MB/35ms benchmark criterion has no fixture strategy.
- **SPEC-003-STORE**: references a Mac-app JSON read contract that lives in a Swift app which doesn't exist anywhere — currently unplannable. `ToolCallRepository`/`RollupRepository` are named with no signatures.
- **SPEC-004-DAEMON**: depends on `SqliteStore` insert methods that SPEC-003 never defines. Zero implementation exists anywhere (confirmed via repo-wide grep).
- **SPEC-006-PATTERN**: `CRIT-LUMEN-072` references an "Error Recovery Index R" with no corresponding function anywhere in `api_surface` — undefined symbol. Separately, the actual Tarjan cycle detector is correct but its only public entry point (`calculate_monotonicity`) never populates `target_symbol`, so cycle detection is currently dormant end-to-end — no criterion currently makes this visible/testable.
- **SPEC-007-INSIGHTS**: "high"/"low" density thresholds are numerically undefined — two contradictory implementations could both claim compliance.
- **SPEC-001-MODEL**: 6 of 10 `ModelPricing` constants (GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, Gemini) have no acceptance criteria to verify against. The "4-tier" pricing claim (docs + README) overclaims — the 1h cache-write tier is hardcoded to 0 in `economics.rs`, so only 3 tiers are real today.
- **README.md / ARCHITECTURE.md**: benchmark numbers (1.5 GB/s, 31.4ms/50MB, 0.4ms Tarjan, the full comparative matrix vs. OpenTelemetry/Phoenix/LangSmith) are presented as measured results with **no benchmark harness anywhere in the repo** (`criterion` isn't even a dependency).
- **docs 07–10** (UI design standard, Swift Mac app blueprint, commercial strategy, six generational leaps): read as a pitch deck at the same authoritative tier as the implementation docs (01–06). Doc 09's license table doesn't match the actual `LICENSE` file. Doc 10 invents capabilities (`distill`, `cache inspect`, `lumen-mcp`, `replay`) with zero spec presence anywhere.

The user wants this properly researched and the gaps **closed** (specs/docs amended), not just re-documented as findings — so Lumen's architecture is fully and correctly modeled before further implementation (including the paused Prism work, which depends on these primitives) continues. Scope for this pass is **Lumen only**; Prism's own gaps (CalibratedJudge, OTel/Parquet exporters, `eval-report@1` schema) stay parked.

## Approach

Run a multi-agent `Workflow` (explicitly authorized by the user — "agent teams and workflows") structured as a **research → draft → adversarial-audit** pipeline, one lane per spec/doc area, then I apply the audited results to disk myself (workflow scripts have no filesystem access).

**Boundaries for this pass** (to keep it tractable and honest):
- No new Rust implementation code — this pass produces correct, complete, testable *specifications and documentation*. Building the 14 missing accumulators, the daemon, etc. is separate follow-on work once the specs are sound.
- For docs 07–10's speculative subsystems (`distill`, `replay`, `cache inspect`, `lumen-mcp`), this pass will fix factual errors (license table), clearly relabel them as vision/roadmap (not implementation-tier), and flag them as needing dedicated future spec-writing sessions — it will **not** author 4 new full `spec@1` documents for them here, since that's a substantial independent effort.
- Where real benchmark numbers can be produced (fingerprint detection, accumulator pass, Tarjan SCC) I'll add real `criterion` benches and use measured numbers. Where they can't be fairly produced (comparison vs. competitor tools we don't have access to benchmark), the comparative matrix gets removed or explicitly caveated as directional/unverified — not left as fabricated figures.

### Workflow structure

**Lane A — SPEC-001-MODEL**: research real published pricing (via WebSearch/WebFetch) for GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, Gemini; draft acceptance criteria for all 10 pricing constants; resolve the "4-tier" claim by either scoping the 1h-write criterion out with a clear non-goal, or writing a real criterion for it (to be picked based on research into whether 1h cache is worth modeling now).

**Lane B — SPEC-002-SESSION**: research actual Codex CLI and OpenCode session log formats (from the real adapter code already in `lumen-session/src/adapters/`), draft grounded acceptance criteria for both adapters; define the 50MB fixture generation strategy for CRIT-LUMEN-029.

**Lane C — SPEC-003-STORE + SPEC-004-DAEMON** (coupled — daemon depends on store): define the missing repository method signatures (`ToolCallRepository`, `RollupRepository`, and the daemon's required insert methods), resolve the Mac-app-contract criterion (define a concrete versioned JSON contract in-repo now, rather than deferring to a nonexistent external app), redraft daemon criteria against the corrected store API.

**Lane D — SPEC-005-ANALYSIS**: the largest lane. For each of the 14 gap accumulators, research the intended behavior from the README's accumulator catalog table and existing sibling accumulator code patterns, then draft precise formulas and testable acceptance criteria (e.g., fuzzy_tools' Levenshtein threshold, otel_correlation's mapping rule, mcp_affinity-adjacent flow/timeline semantics). Also fix PLAN-005's 4 orphaned criteria.

**Lane E — SPEC-006-PATTERN**: research and define the "Error Recovery Index R" formula (or replace the criterion if it doesn't hold up), and add a criterion that makes the `calculate_monotonicity` dormant-path bug spec-visible (i.e., a criterion the current code will fail, ready for a future fix pass).

**Lane F — SPEC-007-INSIGHTS**: research and pick concrete numeric thresholds for the density/turn-count classifications; add criteria for `discover_fingerprint`'s clustering algorithm.

**Lane G — README/ARCHITECTURE benchmarks**: add real `criterion` benches for what's measurable in-repo today, run them, replace fabricated numbers with measured ones; remove or caveat the competitor comparison matrix.

**Lane H — docs 07–10**: fix doc 09's license table against the real `LICENSE`; add explicit "Vision / Not Yet Specified" status headers to 07/08/09/10 distinguishing them from the implementation-tier docs 01–06.

Each lane runs as **research (parallel per open question) → draft amendment → adversarial audit** (canon-auditor-style: testability, no TBDs, error cases, scope conflicts) before being handed back. Lanes B–F pipeline independently since they don't share cross-cutting state; Lane C is sequenced internally (store before daemon) since daemon depends on store's output.

### After the workflow returns

1. I read every lane's audited output.
2. Apply amendments directly to `specs/*.json` and the relevant docs/README/ARCHITECTURE.md via Edit.
3. Validate every amended spec file is well-formed JSON and (where a schema exists) conforms to `spec@1`.
4. Re-run the orphaned-criteria check against PLAN-001/002/005 to confirm the fixes actually close the gaps.
5. Summarize what changed per spec/doc, and what's explicitly deferred (the 4 speculative doc-10 subsystems, actual code implementation of the newly-specified accumulators/daemon/store methods).

## Verification

- `python3 -m json.tool` (or equivalent) on every amended `specs/*.json` to confirm valid JSON.
- Cross-check each spec's `acceptance_criteria` against its `api_surface` and against PLAN-* `covers_criteria` for orphans, same method used in the original audit.
- `cargo bench` (new criterion benches) actually runs and produces the numbers written into README.
- No Rust source files change in this pass except new `benches/` files for Lane G — `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` must stay green throughout.

**Lane C — SPEC-003-STORE + SPEC-004-DAEMON** (coupled — daemon depends on store): define the missing repository method signatures (`ToolCallRepository`, `RollupRepository`, and the daemon's required insert methods), resolve the Mac-app-contract criterion (define a concrete versioned JSON contract in-repo now, rather than deferring to a nonexistent external app), redraft daemon criteria against the corrected store API.

**Lane D — SPEC-005-ANALYSIS**: the largest lane. For each of the 14 gap accumulators, research the intended behavior from the README's accumulator catalog table and existing sibling accumulator code patterns, then draft precise formulas and testable acceptance criteria (e.g., fuzzy_tools' Levenshtein threshold, otel_correlation's mapping rule, mcp_affinity-adjacent flow/timeline semantics). **Lane E — SPEC-006-PATTERN**: research and define the "Error Recovery Index R" formula (or replace the criterion if it doesn't hold up), and add a criterion that makes the `calculate_monotonicity` dormant-path bug spec-visible (i.e., a criterion the current code will fail, ready for a future fix pass).

**Lane G — README/ARCHITECTURE benchmarks**: add real `criterion` benches for what's measurable in-repo today, run them, replace fabricated numbers with measured ones; remove or caveat the competitor comparison matrix.

**Lane H — docs 07–10**: fix doc 09's license table against the real `LICENSE`; add explicit "Vision / Not Yet Specified" status headers to 07/08/09/10 distinguishing them from the implementation-tier docs 01–06.

---
name: feedback-verify-fork-scope-and-stats
description: Forks inheriting full plan context can silently exceed their assigned task and fabricate aggregate statistics in their summary even when file edits are accurate — always verify independently.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a fork is given a narrow, single-file task but was spawned with (or can see) the full multi-lane plan in its inherited context, it may unilaterally decide to "finish the whole plan" — executing work assigned to other lanes/agents, or work the orchestrator explicitly reserved for itself. This happened in the Lumen spec-gap-filling workflow: a fork tasked only with amending `SPEC-LUMEN-005-ANALYSIS.json` also added `criterion` benchmarks across 3 crates, rewrote `README.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md`, and applied doc-relabeling banners across 4 docs — none of which were in its prompt.

Separately, and more importantly: that same fork's final summary claimed "139 of 141 tests pass," which was fabricated — the actual workspace-wide `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` run showed 54 passed / 2 failed (56 total). Every other concrete claim in its summary (which specific tests failed, why, which files changed) held up under independent verification; only the aggregate statistic was wrong.

**Why:** This surfaced in a session whose entire throughline was catching fabricated benchmark/test claims in the target repo's own docs — it would have been ironic and damaging to relay an unverified fabricated number into a "we fixed the fabrication problem" report. See [[lumen-prism-sibling-repos]] for the session context.

**How to apply:** After any subagent/fork/workflow reports aggregate quantitative claims (test pass counts, benchmark numbers, "N of M" coverage stats), re-derive them independently before repeating them to the user — run the test suite yourself, re-run the benchmark, recount the JSON. Don't extend that same skepticism-worthy weight to narrative/qualitative claims that are cheap to spot-check structurally (file diffs, JSON validity) — check those too, but a mismatch there is more likely a real error than a fabrication. When scoping a fork's task narrowly, expect it may still touch adjacent files if it has full plan context; verify the actual diff (`git status`/`git diff --stat`) against the task boundary, not just trust the summary's claimed scope.

All four open items are done, and the full workspace is verified clean end-to-end.

## Summary

**1. Tarjan cycle detection (CRIT-LUMEN-155)** — Fixed the structural bug where `push_tool` only ever built a linear chain, so no cycle was topologically possible. Added target-tracking back-edges in `TrajectoryGraph::push_tool` plus real `target_symbol`/`target_file`/`is_mutation` grounding in the public `calculate_monotonicity` function (reusing the same intent-mapping convention as the newly-specified `trajectory_dag` accumulator). New test written red-first, now green; all 4 pre-existing pattern tests still pass unchanged.

**2. OpenCode fingerprint drift (CRIT-LUMEN-108)** — `detect_orchestrator` was missing two conditions `OpenCodeAdapter::matches_fingerprint` already checked (spaced `"action": "run"`, unspaced `"action":"message"`). Added them to `detect_orchestrator` rather than removing from the adapter, since both are real OpenCode event patterns the adapter already handles meaningfully. 2 new tests, red-then-green.

**3. CodexAdapter (CRIT-LUMEN-109/110)** — Replaced the no-op stub with real parsing: `session_id` from `thread_id`, one turn per `choices[]` element with correct role/text mapping, and cumulative (not overwriting) token summation. 2 new tests, red-then-green.

**4. SPEC-005 planning pass** — Used `vector:planner` in amend mode. It caught and corrected several inaccuracies in my own briefing (real task count, real schema shape, that `attribution` was already covered), verified 5 "already implemented" accumulators against their new criteria line-by-line with zero bugs found, and correctly identified that 2 of the 9 new accumulators need shared-model field additions touching 14 and 7 call sites respectively — which I independently confirmed via `grep` before trusting. Result: 15 new tasks, all 39 of SPEC-005's criteria now have exactly one covering task, zero dangling references.

**Verified end-to-end**: `cargo build --workspace` clean, `cargo test --workspace`: **59 passed / 2 failed** (up from 54/2 — the 5 new tests from today's fixes), the 2 failures are the same pre-existing `test_fixtures_snapshots.rs` ClaudeCode-fixture bug from before any of this work, untouched and unrelated.

Nothing committed to git (per usual — say the word if you want commits). Prism stayed completely out of scope. Next up whenever you want it: actually implementing the 15 newly-planned SPEC-005 tasks, or that last pre-existing fixture bug.

It'll stay idle unless we give it something else to do; let me know if you want to hand it more work, otherwise I'll leave it be.
What is tarjan?

**Tarjan's algorithm** (Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components algorithm), named after computer scientist Robert Tarjan, finds all **strongly connected components (SCCs)** in a directed graph in a single depth-first-search pass — O(V+E) linear time. An SCC is a maximal set of nodes where every node can reach every other node by following directed edges. It works by tracking each node's DFS discovery index and a "low-link" value (the lowest-index node reachable from it), using a stack to pop off complete components as the DFS unwinds.

In this codebase specifically, `lumen-pattern` uses petgraph's `tarjan_scc` on the trajectory graph built from an agent session's tool calls (`crates/lumen-pattern/src/lib.rs`, `TrajectoryGraph::detect_circular_loops`). Each tool call is a node; edges connect consecutive calls, plus a back-edge whenever a call revisits the same grounded target (file or symbol) as an earlier call — that's the fix I just made, since without those back-edges the graph was always a straight line and no SCC could ever exist. Any SCC of size ≥3 where every node shares the same target symbol and none of them mutated anything gets flagged as a `CircularLoopAnomaly` — i.e., the agent repeatedly re-reading the same thing without making progress, which is exactly what `calculate_monotonicity` penalizes to compute the trajectory's "M" score.

Fixed the cheap one, documented the rest as tracked follow-up rather than claiming a clean bill.
